paper_a.title: Deep Reinforcement Learning with Double Q-learning (van Hasselt, Guez, Silver, 2015)

paper_b.title: Playing Atari with Deep Reinforcement Learning (Mnih et al., 2013)

metadata.description: Double DQN is a bug-fix / improvement to DQN. It identifies and corrects the systematic overestimation bias in DQN's Q-value estimates by decoupling action selection from action evaluation using the already-existing target network. The fix requires changing only a single line of code in DQN.

matches.explanation: Both define the Q-learning target. DQN uses $Y = r + \gamma \max_{a'} Q(s', a'; \theta^-)$ which Double DQN identifies as the source of overestimation. Double DQN's analysis of the max operator bias directly references and critiques this DQN target formulation.

Double DQN reuses the exact DQN architecture (same convolutional network) and the DQN training algorithm (experience replay, target network). The only change is replacing the target $\max_a Q(s', a; \theta^-)$ with $Q(s', \arg\max_a Q(s', a; \theta); \theta^-)$. The target network $\theta^-$, which DQN introduced for stability, is repurposed for evaluation while the online network handles selection.
The standard DQN target $Y^{\mathrm{DQN}} = r + \gamma \max_a Q(s', a; \theta^-)$ is reproduced in the Double DQN paper as the baseline to be improved. Identical equation.

The Double DQN target $Y^{\mathrm{DoubleDQN}} = r + \gamma Q(s', \arg\max_a Q(s', a; \theta); \theta^-)$ is the novel contribution: decoupling selection (online $\theta$) from evaluation (target $\theta^-$). Not present in DQN.
Experience replay is a core DQN contribution. Double DQN inherits it without modification but does not present it as a contribution.
Frame preprocessing and stacking is DQN infrastructure. Double DQN uses it unchanged.

Both report Atari game performance. DQN reports superhuman performance on 3/7 games; Double DQN extends evaluation to 49 games and shows substantial improvement over DQN, with median score increasing from 68% to 116% of human performance.
